rv.q: For me, Pilkey’s wildest plot twists come over as merely bewildering here.
Still: it's charming and it's done with heart. It's not trying to cynically cash in on a popular IP.

But as the energetic cast dance, sing and bark their way around the set like CBeebies presenters after three pints of Skittles, these more moving moments get buried in the production, directed and choreographed by Jen Wineman.
Dog Man: The Musical is a joy as it never underestimates its audience.
The show is short (but performed across two acts) and silly – just as it should be.
However, if you’re just looking for some lo-fi family-friendly fun with a few good songs, I’d hold on for panto season.

Everything’s incredibly low-tech, from the colourful, cardboard-themed set (designed by Timothy R Macabee) to the puppets used to depict Flippy the evil fish being dropped into the Living Spray Factory.
No matter your age, Dog Man: The Musical is a perfect treat, hilarious and whimsical, crafty and smart.
If your child loves Dog Man books, they’ll love this too.
Perhaps my main concern is whether Dog Man truly needs to be a musical.
Based on four of Dav Pilkey’s immensely popular graphic Dog Man stories, this is a decent enough children’s musical (by Kevin Del Aguila and Brad Alexander) although it’s unremarkable.
As children’s musicals go, Dog Man the Musical is no Matilda.

cn.t: Critics find this adaptation of Dav Pilkey's beloved books captures the source material's chaotic energy and playfulness, though reactions are mixed on execution. Young fans will likely enjoy it more than adults, with standout performances noted.
